title: Birth in Galveston and hearing bands at father's pawn shop
summary: Manno gives his birth details, then recalls bands playing at the dance hall above his father's pawn shop and musicians practising in the back room. He remembers Peck Kelly's band later but not names of the bands' members.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: okay it's going all right let's let's get your name first Len. My name is Len Mano now of course that's the name that I go by but my name is really Leonard Wilbur Mano and I shudder every time I say Wilbur now where were you born well I was born in Galveston Texas on Monday July the 5th 1915
right after lunch and let's see what was the first music you ever heard by the way over there well the

first music that I can really remember was down on West Market in Galveston where my father had a pawn shop he had a pawn shop down at 2509 West Market and just above that they had this colored dance hall and of course back in those days of the old Louie and King Oliver and well those are the two outstanding names as far as I'm concerned with Louie and King Oliver would play for dances over there every Saturday night they had dances and they brought musicians and all over the South but they all came into the store and traded with my father usually it was Monday morning where they come in to hock their horns and then take them back out Friday Saturday and then of course sometime during the week they used to come in and say Mr. Leo can we come in and practice a little bit we know we can't take our horns out but can we practice and he had a pretty good sized room in the back of the store and they used to let him practice back there and of course that's one way that I got closer to them and really got chance to listen to them and then on Saturday afternoons they would get on this truck and go all through the color district back in those days we call it nigger town and they used to go all up and down through there and and ballyhoo ballyhoo and they used to let me sit up on top of the piano it was up in the front of the truck how old were you I imagine I must have been about six or seven so you really heard great bands when you were young oh yes oh yes and then the next music that I can remember was when Peck Kelly had Peck's bad boys he had Jack T Gordon and Charlie T Gordon and then there there was Sammy Bird drummer who is more or less local he's pretty well known all up and down the Gulf Coast there and Galveston and coppers and all down the valley but of course Peck and the tea gardens and Sam were really the only ones that I can remember real clear
let me turn it off for just a second well do you remember any of the fellows that were in King Oliver's band or Louis Armstrong's band

no I can't remember them at all and actually the name in those days Louis Armstrong really didn't mean too much to me it was it was in later years that I realized that it was Louis and oh and King Oliver and those fellows that I've been listening to back back in those days well it was just a matter of fact uh they were just another band there on Saturday night just some guy named Joe I mean you didn't know
